# RFC-0002: Agent-Ergonomic MCP Service Contract

> **Version:** 0.1.0 | **Status:** draft | **Phase:** spec
> **Owners:** @Tyler Michael Smith

---

## 1. Summary

### [RFC-0002:C-PURPOSE] Purpose and caller model (Informative) <a id="rfc-0002c-purpose"></a>

This RFC defines cross-cutting usability and safety requirements for every MCP service in nm-hard-tools. The primary caller is an autonomous agent that must understand a tool from its advertised contract, make safe choices with limited context, recover from failure, and interpret results without repository or implementation knowledge. Domain RFCs remain responsible for each service's concrete goals, tool surface, payload format, and operational semantics.

### [RFC-0002:C-SCOPE] Scope and non-goals (Informative) <a id="rfc-0002c-scope"></a>

This RFC governs MCP discovery, tool metadata, input ergonomics, configuration-document handling, results, errors, safety, compatibility, and capability-appropriate inspection across all nm-hard-tools MCP services. It permits both single-tool direct-action services and multi-tool lifecycle services. It does not require every service to expose planning, asynchronous status, cancellation, listings, artifacts, inspection, or comparison. This RFC does not prescribe private types, Kubernetes layouts, REST routes, storage engines, deployment topology, or implementation language.

---

## 2. Specification

### [RFC-0002:C-AUTHORITY] Umbrella and domain authority (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-authority"></a>

Every nm-hard-tools MCP service MUST satisfy the applicable cross-cutting obligations of this RFC. Domain RFCs own concrete service goals, tool names and cardinality, payload and result schemas, operational semantics, and domain error codes. A domain RFC MAY strengthen this RFC but MUST NOT silently weaken an applicable obligation. An incompatibility MUST be resolved by amending the governing RFCs rather than by implicit precedence.

### [RFC-0002:C-SERVICE-BOUNDARIES] Bounded domain services (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-service-boundaries"></a>

Each MCP server MUST represent a coherent operator-owned domain and MUST identify that domain in its advertised server name and instructions. A server MUST expose the smallest tool surface that completes its supported caller goals within one authorization and operational boundary. A service MAY expose one direct-action tool, a lifecycle-oriented family, or another domain-appropriate surface. A server MUST NOT expose an internal route or operation solely because it exists, and a caller MUST NOT need knowledge of controllers, Jobs, filenames, or storage layout to choose a tool.

### [RFC-0002:C-PROTOCOL-DISCOVERY] Protocol and server discovery (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-protocol-discovery"></a>

Each server MUST support MCP protocol version `2026-07-28`. Its `server/discover` result MUST expose `supportedVersions`, `capabilities`, `instructions`, `ttlMs`, and `cacheScope` as defined by that protocol version. Every result MUST expose the stable server name and service version in `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo"].name` and `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo"].version`. Advertised capabilities MUST match the methods and content types the server actually supports. Requests MUST be independent of conversational or transport session state; any state needed by a later call MUST be represented by an explicit opaque reference returned to the caller. Server instructions MUST state the preferred workflow, the authorization boundary, and the result-size strategy in no more than 1,024 Unicode characters.

### [RFC-0002:C-TOOL-FAMILIES] Common tool families (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-tool-families"></a>

Tool names MUST use verb-first snake_case and describe complete caller goals in domain language. Related tools MUST use consistent nouns and identifiers. A direct-action service MAY expose a single tool when one bounded call can validate, execute, and return the useful outcome. A service that exposes separate discovery, planning, execution, status, cancellation, artifact, inspection, or comparison operations MUST make their sequence and shared identifiers evident from tool names, descriptions, and results. Domain RFCs own exact tool names and cardinality.

### [RFC-0002:C-CAPABILITY-CATALOG] Discoverable operator capabilities (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-capability-catalog"></a>

When caller-selectable valid input depends on dynamic choices or constraints not represented by the advertised input contract, the service MUST expose a bounded read-only discovery mechanism through an MCP tool or resource. Discovery MUST return stable machine identifiers, caller-facing descriptions, defaults, bounds, mutually dependent constraints, enabled optional features, and a minimal valid example or template. Operator-controlled values that callers cannot select MUST NOT trigger discovery and MUST NOT be enumerated. For a configuration-document field, the metadata required by [RFC-0002:C-CONFIGURATION-DOCUMENTS](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-configuration-documents), an advertised schema authority or pinned consumer version, and a bounded valid example MAY satisfy discovery without adding another tool. Large discovery results MUST support filtering or cursor pagination and MUST report omitted content.

### [RFC-0002:C-TOOL-METADATA] Tool selection metadata (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-tool-metadata"></a>

Every tool MUST provide a stable name, title, description, input schema, output schema when it returns structured content, and truthful MCP annotations. An output schema MUST accept every structured success and tool-error variant the tool can return. A description MUST say when to use the tool, its material side effect or lack thereof, its principal prerequisite, and what the successful result enables. `readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`, `idempotentHint`, and `openWorldHint` MUST accurately describe observable behavior. Tools MUST be returned in deterministic name order.

### [RFC-0002:C-INPUT-SCHEMAS] Agent-constructible inputs (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-input-schemas"></a>

Every tool input MUST be a closed JSON object that rejects unknown top-level properties. Fixed semantic values SHOULD use typed structured fields with explicit formats, enums for closed choices, unit-bearing names, documented defaults, and descriptions where meaning is not evident. A tool MAY use a bounded configuration document string as its primary domain payload when an extensible external or operator-pinned schema is the authoritative representation; such inputs MUST satisfy [RFC-0002:C-CONFIGURATION-DOCUMENTS](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-configuration-documents). Tool inputs MUST NOT accept shell fragments, arbitrary command-line arguments, credentials, or an encoded private request representation.

### [RFC-0002:C-CONFIGURATION-DOCUMENTS] Agent-usable configuration documents (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-configuration-documents"></a>

Metadata for a primary configuration-document field MUST appear in its input-property description or in a stable descriptor referenced from tool metadata or server instructions and retrievable before invocation. That metadata MUST declare the document media type or language, maximum UTF-8 byte size, document-count limit, schema authority or pinned consumer version, and handling of aliases, duplicate keys, custom tags, inheritance, and unknown fields. Parsing MUST be safe and resource-bounded by depth, expanded nodes, execution time, or equivalent limits appropriate to the format. Validation MUST occur before external mutation. Rejections SHOULD identify a semantic path and source line or column when safely available. The service MUST distinguish a digest of exact submitted bytes from any identity derived from the accepted semantic form. Holding the schema or pinned consumer version and every domain-declared operator-controlled identity input constant, documents whose accepted semantic forms differ only in formatting MUST derive the same semantic identity when the service claims idempotent convergence. A domain RFC MUST define ignored or overridden document fields and any operator-controlled inputs included in that identity. Planning or success results SHOULD expose a bounded canonical summary, resolved defaults, stable identity, or digest sufficient to confirm what the service accepted without echoing the complete document. A service MUST NOT require a reduced structured alternative that cannot represent every configuration accepted by the authoritative schema.

### [RFC-0002:C-PLAN] Exact preview before mutation (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-plan"></a>

A service SHOULD expose a read-only planning operation when a mutation is expensive, asynchronous, difficult to reverse, or materially affected by resolved defaults that are not visible in the submitted input. Satisfying all of the following conditions is an accepted reason not to expose a separate planning operation: the complete caller-controlled intent is visible before invocation; execution has a domain-governed finite bound; repeated calls converge idempotently; and failure before target acceptance leaves external state unchanged. When planning is exposed, its result MUST show the resolved intent, material resources and placement, warnings, stable digest, and expiration when applicable without performing the mutation.

### [RFC-0002:C-SUBMIT] Plan-bound idempotent submission (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-submit"></a>

When execution is separated from planning, the execution tool MUST accept an opaque reference to the exact plan and MUST NOT require the caller to repeat the planned payload. The first successful execution of a plan reference MUST bind it atomically to one domain operation or result. Concurrent and later authorized retries MUST return or reconcile that same operation or result. Expiry and feasibility checks apply only before the first successful binding. A direct-action tool MUST derive a stable semantic identity when it advertises `idempotentHint: true` or its domain RFC requires retries or equivalent concurrent calls to converge. The domain RFC MUST define the semantic input and operator-controlled identity context. Repeated equivalent calls under the same identity context MUST reconcile one logical operation or result.

### [RFC-0002:C-OPERATION-STATUS] Self-contained asynchronous status (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-operation-status"></a>

When a service returns a handle for asynchronous work, status results MUST include a stable domain identifier, machine-readable state, whether the state is terminal, creation and update times when available, a concise summary, and safe available actions. Nonterminal status MUST provide a polling recommendation or advertised event mechanism. Terminal status MUST identify the availability of its useful result and artifacts. Domain RFCs own the state vocabulary and transitions, but terminal states MUST NOT silently become nonterminal.

### [RFC-0002:C-LIST] Bounded resumable listing (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-list"></a>

When a service exposes operation or result listing, each response MUST be bounded and deterministically ordered. A listing that can exceed one response MUST use opaque cursor pagination over a stable traversal snapshot or another documented consistency mechanism that prevents gaps and duplicates. The result MUST state whether more items exist and provide a continuation when they do. Invalid or expired continuation state MUST produce an actionable tool error that lets the caller restart safely.

### [RFC-0002:C-CANCELLATION] Safe cancellation semantics (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-cancellation"></a>

When a service exposes cancellation, cancellation MUST be idempotent and MUST preserve enough operation identity and outcome information for later inspection. Cancelling terminal work MUST return its current status without changing it. Cancelling active work MUST distinguish requested, in-progress, and durable cancellation rather than claiming completion prematurely. A cancellation tool MUST set `destructiveHint` to true because it stops intended work.

### [RFC-0002:C-RESULT-REPRESENTATION] Token-efficient structured results (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-result-representation"></a>

Every returned `structuredContent` value MUST conform to the tool's advertised output schema. Successful and error results MUST be distinguishable by the MCP `isError` value and by non-overlapping schema variants when both are structured. Text content MUST be a concise caller-facing summary and SHOULD NOT duplicate the complete structured result for protocol version `2026-07-28`. Versioned domain results MUST include a schema version. Timestamps, byte counts, durations, rates, units, and identifiers MUST have unambiguous representations.

### [RFC-0002:C-BOUNDED-RESULTS] Progressive disclosure and result bounds (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-bounded-results"></a>

Every tool result MUST be bounded by an advertised or domain-governed limit. A service SHOULD return a useful summary, pagination, a narrower follow-up action, or an artifact reference instead of only an oversize error when a bounded representation is available. Results MUST state when matching evidence is omitted, sampled, approximate, stale, or otherwise incomplete and MUST explain the limitation. Pagination state MUST be distinct from evidence completeness.

### [RFC-0002:C-ARTIFACTS] Artifact-oriented detail access (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-artifacts"></a>

When a service exposes artifacts, it MUST identify them with stable authorized references and bounded metadata sufficient to choose a follow-up action. Metadata SHOULD include semantic kind, media type, byte size, digest, schema identity when structured, creation or modification time, retention information, and supported inspection or retrieval actions when applicable. Services SHOULD return semantic summaries before raw bulky content. Artifact access MUST preserve authorization, MUST NOT expose credentials or private storage paths, and MUST distinguish expired references from invalid requests without leaking unauthorized existence.

### [RFC-0002:C-ERRORS] Actionable stable errors (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-errors"></a>

Invalid MCP envelopes, authentication or authorization failures before invocation, unknown tools, unsupported methods, and protocol negotiation failures MUST use protocol-level errors. A recognized tool domain failure MUST return `isError: true`; when structured, its error object MUST conform to the advertised output schema and include stable `code`, concise `message`, and `retryable`. Validation errors SHOULD identify semantic field or document locations and violated constraints. Retryable errors SHOULD include retry timing when known. State conflicts and recoverable failures SHOULD include a safe suggested action when one exists. Domain RFCs own their error-code vocabulary and MAY require additional identity or acceptance fields. Errors MUST NOT expose credentials, submitted configuration documents, stack traces, internal network locations, or unbounded dependency output.

### [RFC-0002:C-AUTHORIZATION] Authorization and open-world safety (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-authorization"></a>

Servers MUST authenticate and authorize requests before parsing sensitive domain payloads when authentication is configured. Tool results and discovery MUST reveal only choices, operations, and artifacts authorized for the caller. The service MUST keep credentials, target environments, namespaces, deployment identity, storage roots, and other operator controls outside caller input unless a domain RFC explicitly delegates a bounded choice. A tool MUST set `openWorldHint` to true when caller input can cause interaction with externally selected or non-local destinations and false otherwise.

### [RFC-0002:C-COMPATIBILITY] Compatibility and evolution (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-compatibility"></a>

Published tool names, required input fields, payload meanings, identifier meanings, error-code meanings, and structured output fields MUST remain backward compatible within a service major version. Additive optional fields MAY be introduced within a major version. Adding or changing a closed output value is breaking unless unknown-value handling was part of the original contract. Configuration-document schema authority and versioning MUST be advertised or pinned so callers can distinguish compatible inputs. A breaking change MUST use a new major version or tool name and provide a documented migration path.

### [RFC-0002:C-CONFORMANCE] Agent-journey conformance (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-conformance"></a>

Each service MUST maintain automated conformance coverage selected from the capabilities it advertises. Every service MUST cover discovery or self-description, valid invocation, unknown input rejection, truthful annotations, bounded success, a bounded domain failure, authorization behavior when configured, idempotency when claimed, and result-schema conformance. When a tool advertises or returns structured domain errors, tests MUST validate those errors against the advertised output schema. A configuration-document tool that advertises `idempotentHint: true` or whose domain RFC requires convergence MUST test exact-byte digest behavior separately from semantic identity, including formatting-equivalent documents under the same operator identity context. Every configuration-document tool MUST additionally cover safe parsing, bounds, schema rejection, and redaction. A lifecycle service MUST cover nonmutating planning when exposed, retry convergence, resumption, terminal-state behavior, and cancellation when exposed. Listing and inspection capabilities MUST cover pagination recovery and provenance; comparison capabilities MUST cover alignment, units, missing values, and incompatibility.

---

## 3. Result Inspection

### [RFC-0002:C-INSPECTION-MODEL] Layered result inspection (Informative) <a id="rfc-0002c-inspection-model"></a>

When a service produces complex results or artifacts, agents should normally inspect semantic questions such as outcome, metrics, failure, configuration, or provenance rather than storage filenames and serialization details. A service may provide semantic result views, bounded structured artifact queries, raw resource access, or only a bounded final result according to domain need. The inspection surface should expose the least detail needed first and retain a path to exact evidence when that evidence exists.

### [RFC-0002:C-INSPECTION-DISCOVERY] Discoverable inspection views (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-inspection-discovery"></a>

When a service exposes multiple semantic result views, it MUST make supported views discoverable through tool metadata, a bounded capability result, or an MCP resource. Each view descriptor MUST identify its stable name, purpose, applicable result states or kinds, accepted parameters, returned data shape, result bounds, and whether data is live, immutable, comparable, sampled, or approximate. Schemas MAY be embedded or referenced through a stable authorized MCP resource. Domain RFCs own view identifiers, measures, alignment keys, units, and compatibility rules.

### [RFC-0002:C-SEMANTIC-INSPECTION] Semantic result inspection (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-semantic-inspection"></a>

A semantic inspection tool MUST accept a stable domain result or operation reference plus a discoverable view or question selector. It MUST validate view parameters against the advertised contract. A successful result MUST identify the subject, selected view, snapshot or observation time, bounded data, evidence completeness, and source artifacts or domain evidence when available. A request made before evidence can exist MUST return a distinguishable not-ready error; an applicable view with no matching evidence MUST return a valid empty result. Read-only inspection MUST be annotated accordingly.

### [RFC-0002:C-INSPECTION-PAGINATION] Stable inspection pagination (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-inspection-pagination"></a>

An inspection, artifact query, or comparison whose result can exceed one response MUST provide deterministic bounded traversal. Opaque cursor pagination SHOULD let a continuation call pass only the cursor rather than repeat the original query. A cursor MUST preserve the original subject, authorization scope, query, schemas, ordering, and page size. Invalid or expired cursors MUST fail safely and SHOULD provide a restart action that does not include sensitive input.

### [RFC-0002:C-ARTIFACT-QUERY] Bounded structured artifact queries (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-artifact-query"></a>

When a service exposes structured artifact queries, every supported query mode MUST be declarative, bounded, and discoverable. Its contract MUST describe accepted parameters, result shape, defaults, ordering, page or byte limits, scan or execution limits, and supported artifact kinds. Query inputs MUST NOT execute shell fragments, arbitrary code, or an unrestricted implementation-specific query language. The result MUST identify the artifact and digest or immutable version, normalized query, bounded data, completeness, and continuation when applicable. Exceeding a statically checkable bound MUST fail before expensive work with an actionable validation error; reaching a runtime bound MUST not return an unmarked partial result.

### [RFC-0002:C-RESULT-COMPARISON] Cross-operation comparison (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-result-comparison"></a>

When a service exposes comparison, the input MUST identify the compared results and an explicit baseline or another unambiguous comparison relation. The comparison contract MUST define compatibility fields, alignment keys or aggregation, comparable measures, units, missing-value behavior, and any absolute, relative, improvement, or regression semantics. Required incompatibility MUST fail with per-result diagnostics. Report-only differences MUST remain visible. Large comparisons MUST be bounded and resumable or expose a bounded projection.

### [RFC-0002:C-INSPECTION-PROVENANCE] Inspection evidence and explainability (Normative) <a id="rfc-0002c-inspection-provenance"></a>

Every derived inspection or comparison result MUST identify its subject identities, source artifact or result versions when available, schema or interpretation version, effective query parameters, and snapshot time. Derived, sampled, approximate, or incomplete values MUST identify the method and source fields or evidence needed to interpret them. Service-generated summaries MUST distinguish observed facts from derived values and MUST NOT present unsupported causal explanations as evidence.
